metadata.name: blkid
metadata.description: Show filesystem type, UUID, and label for block devices

installation.note: blkid is typically available by default as part of util-linux on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: The blkid command reports attributes of block devices such as filesystem type, UUID, and labels. It's frequently used when configuring /etc/fstab, troubleshooting mounts, or identifying partitions in a stable way (UUIDs are more reliable than /dev/sdX names).
when_to_use: Troubleshoot mount errors (wrong fs type, bad superblock, etc.)

syntax.description: Without DEVICE, blkid prints attributes for all detected devices (permission-dependent). You can also query a specific device path like /dev/sda1.

options.description: Show only the specified tag (e.g., UUID, TYPE, LABEL)
options.use_case: When you only need one attribute

options.description: Choose output format (e.g., full, value, export)
options.use_case: For scripting (get a raw UUID string)

options.description: Low-level probe (may be slower; bypass cache)
options.use_case: When cached info seems stale or incorrect

examples.title: List all block devices with attributes
examples.description: Print UUID, type, and label for detected block devices

examples.title: Extract just the UUID for a device
examples.description: Output only the UUID value (useful in scripts)
examples.use_case: Copy the UUID into /etc/fstab or a mount script

common_pitfalls.description: Some devices may not be visible without elevated permissions.
common_pitfalls.solution: Use sudo (e.g., sudo blkid) when querying all devices.

common_pitfalls.description: /dev/sda, /dev/sdb ordering can change, especially with USB disks.
common_pitfalls.solution: Prefer UUIDs or labels (from blkid/lsblk -f) in /etc/fstab.
